source.title: Tracking Universal Features Through Fine-Tuning and Model Merging

record.file_problem: The opening of the abstract appears truncated or garbled, and some figure layouts are flattened in the supplied text. The main methods, results, conclusion, and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether SAE features persist and recur in the new setting of domain fine-tuning and model merging.
record.gate_note: Rows record feature persistence, emergence, and cross-model feature-pattern correlations reported by the study. The interpolation accuracy curve is not a feature-alignment result. The figure-only flow labels are not separately recorded because their paths cannot be assigned reliably from the flattened figure text.
record.test_reason: The study correlates SAE feature activation patterns across a family of related models: a base model, two domain fine-tunes and a SLERP merge. Its results show whether the same interpretable features recur across these models (V5), in the new setting of shared-base fine-tuning and merging. It does not compare independently trained models or seeds, vary scale or metric, or measure causes of overlap.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right, but incomplete. The authors find very few features persist across the related models. Those that persist are interpretable and generic, such as punctuation and formatting. SLERP merging can maintain parent features, while fine-tuning and merging dilute them. The claim that correlations are weaker than for identically trained Transformers is asserted without a measured comparison.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SAE feature activation-pattern correlations and an 80% persistence threshold, following the general approach of Bricken et al.; studies fine-tuning and merging of small language models rather than scale convergence across independent model families.
record.method_sensitivity: Persistence is defined using a correlation threshold greater than 80%, selected after manual inspection; the study does not vary this threshold or compare similarity measures.
record.code_released: The authors say code and weights will be available upon publication; no URL is stated.
record.problems: The study uses small one-layer models in limited English and programming-language domains. Models share a base checkpoint, so the study does not establish feature universality across independent model families. It reports no uncertainty estimates for the feature counts or correlations, and the persistence count depends on a manually selected threshold.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 2 contains flow labels and counts, but their paths cannot be assigned reliably from the flattened figure text. Figure 3 shows individual assignment-feature correlations, but the text reports the aggregate mean cross-correlation instead. Figure 5 reports validation accuracy over interpolation fractions, which does not measure feature convergence.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep; no independently trained models.
No vision-language or paired cross-modal data.
No models trained from different initializations; all models share one base checkpoint.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation test.
Single similarity measure and a fixed 80% threshold chosen by inspection; threshold, metric and inputs are not varied.

Models are fine-tuned derivatives of one base, so incomplete persistence is not partial convergence of independent models. Causes of overlap are not tested. The comparison to identically trained Transformers is asserted, not measured.

record.verdict_notes: Only V5 is tested, and in a weak sense: the 'different models' are fine-tuned or merged derivatives of one base, not independent models. Figure 2 flow shares (about 1–3.5% per path) and the Figure 3 per-pair correlations (80–94%) are declared in rows_left_out; adding them would strengthen the rows. The persistence threshold is a single manually chosen value, and no uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep across independently trained models.
No paired image-caption or other vision-language representations.
Models share a base checkpoint and are fine-tuned or merged; the study does not compare independently initialized seeds or shared subspaces across seeds.
The study correlates SAE feature activation patterns; it does not test mapping representations, stitching layers, relative representations, or unpaired mappings.
Tests SAE features, not recurring neurons or circuits. The study is limited to small one-layer language models and these training settings.
Uses an 80% correlation threshold but does not vary the similarity measure, its settings, or the input distribution to test metric or data dependence.
Reports incomplete persistence in related fine-tuned and merged models, but does not test whether shared training data or objectives cause the overlap, nor whether alignment plateaus.

rows.subject: BabyPython → Lua and TinyStories (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned the shared BabyPython base separately on Lua and TinyStories, then counted features persisting from the base.
rows.measure: Number of BabyPython features persisting into either fine-tuned model
rows.note: The study reports the combined count for either fine-tuned model, not separate counts for Lua and TinyStories.
rows.check: Linked to V7 without basis. The models share a base checkpoint, so limited persistence under fine-tuning is feature drift, not incomplete convergence between independent models. The row lacks a denominator: each SAE has 16×1024 = 16,384 features, so 959 is about 6%, which the authors call 'very few features persist'.

rows.subject: LuaStories
rows.operation_detail: Merged the Lua and TinyStories fine-tuned models using spherical linear interpolation and traced features to the source models.
rows.measure: Number of features traced back to either Lua or TinyStories
rows.note: Reported as an aggregate across the two source models.
rows.check: Remove the V7 link for the same shared-base reason. The denominator is about 16,384 features per SAE, so 1,210 traced features is a small share.

rows.subject: LuaStories
rows.operation_detail: Counted features in the merged model that emerged during fine-tuning.
rows.measure: Number of features classified as emerged during fine-tuning
rows.note: The result indicates that many final-model features were not traced to the base model.
rows.check: Remove the V7 link. The 729 features are a subset of r2: features that emerged in the fine-tunes and persist into the merge. The row's note misreads this as features 'not traced'.

rows.subject: LuaStories
rows.operation_detail: Counted features in the merged model that persisted from the initial BabyPython model.
rows.measure: Number of features persisting from BabyPython
rows.note: The study describes most base-model features as disappearing through fine-tuning.
rows.check: Remove the V7 link. This is 481 of about 16,384 base features (about 3%), and a subset of r2.

relationships.condition: Overall feature recurrence across shared-base fine-tuned and merged one-layer models
relationships.reason: Only 959 of about 16,384 base features persist into either fine-tune, and 481 into the merge (r1, r4). The Python exception feature does not recur (40.81%, r10). Recurrence is the exception, not the rule, even in closely related models.
relationships.display_finding: Only 959 of approximately 16,384 base features persisted into either fine-tune and 481 into the merge; the Python exception feature failed to recur at 40.81% correlation.
